newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER-MANDELA INVITES GULLIT TO PLAY IN S.AFRICA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MANDELA INVITES GULLIT TO PLAY IN S.AFRICA.

text.p: Chelsea's player-coach Ruud Gullit has been asked by Nelson Mandela to return to the Dutch national team for a special friendly match against South Africa in June, the Dutch Soccer Union KNVB said.
"Gullit has received an invitation, but so far we don't know if he will accept it," a spokeswoman for the KNVB said.
The friendly international in Johannesburg on June 1 is billed as the Nelson Mandela Inauguration Challenge, an annual event since 1994.

Gullit has in the past professed huge admiration for the South African leader. In 1987, when the former Feyenoord and AC Milan player was named European Footballer of the Year, he dedicated his prize to Mandela, at the time still in prison.

Gullit has said an invitation from Mandela would be a great honour and one he would be pleased to accept, assuming he recovers from the ankle injury which has ruled him out of the rest of Chelsea's matches this season.
He has not played for the Dutch national team since he walked away out of preparations ahead of the 1994 World Cup in the United States after a disagreement over tactics.
